title: Solids and Liquids
seo_title: Grade 2 Science: Solids and Liquids Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Identify properties of solids and liquids; describe how liquids flow and take the shape of their container; describe what happens when solids and liquids are mixed. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Properties of Liquids and Solids)
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 science worksheets on solids, liquids, how liquids flow, floating and sinking and mixing, with pictures. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow.
key_sub: Liquids take the shape of their container. Some solids dissolve in water.
body_html:
How to think about it

Solids keep their shape. Liquids flow and take the shape of their container.

  • Rocks, blocks and ice are solids.
  • Water, milk and syrup are liquids.
  • Sugar dissolves in water; sand does not.
Example

Is milk a solid or a liquid?

it can be poured

Answer: a liquid

Example

Does sand dissolve?

it sinks

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sand is a liquid because it can be poured.
  • Thinking dissolved sugar is gone.

faq.q: What is the difference between a solid and a liquid?
faq.a: A solid keeps its own shape. A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.
A solid mixes into a liquid so you cannot see it, like sugar in water.

items.q: What happens when oil is poured into water?
items.e: Oil and water do not mix.

items.q: Which one is a liquid?
items.e: Liquids flow and take the shape of their container.

items.q: Leah looks at snow on a mountain top. Is this water solid or liquid?
c: It is a gas you can see.
items.e: Snow on a mountain top is solid water.

items.q: Which is a solid that can bend?
items.e: Some solids are bendy.

items.q: Leah looks at a snowflake. Is this water solid or liquid?
c: It is a gas you can see.
items.e: A snowflake is solid water.

items.q: Is butter (from the fridge) a solid, a liquid or a gas?
items.e: Butter (from the fridge) is a solid.

items.q: Is the air inside a soccer ball a solid, a liquid or a gas?
items.e: The air inside a soccer ball is a gas.

items.q: Which of these is a solid: sand, shampoo, the air inside a soccer ball or the bubbles in a pop?
c: the air inside a soccer ball
items.e: Each grain is a hard solid that keeps its shape; the grains just pour.

items.q: Which of these is a solid: helium in a balloon, sugar, the air inside a soccer ball or water?
c: the air inside a soccer ball
items.e: Each grain is a solid; the grains pour.

items.q: Which of these is a gas: flour, milk, steam or sugar?
items.e: Steam is a gas.

items.q: Is a stone a solid, a liquid or a gas?
items.e: A stone is a solid.

items.q: What does a liquid do when you pour it into a new cup?
c: It takes the shape of the cup.
items.e: Liquids flow.

items.q: Nathan looks at a waterfall. Is this water solid or liquid?
c: It is a gas you can see.
items.e: A waterfall is liquid water.

items.q: How does Maya know a waterfall is liquid water?
c: It is liquid, so it flows.
It is cold, so it is not water.
It is solid, so it keeps its own shape.
items.e: Solids keep their shape. Liquids flow.

items.q: Which of these is a solid: helium in a balloon, milk, salt or water vapour?
items.e: Salt grains are tiny solids.

items.q: Which of these is a liquid: a glass marble, a stone, milk or steam?
items.e: Milk is a liquid.

items.q: Which one floats on water?
items.e: Light objects can float.

items.q: How does Noah know rain is liquid water?
c: It is liquid, so it flows.
It is cold, so it is not water.
It is solid, so it keeps its own shape.
items.e: Solids keep their shape. Liquids flow.

items.q: Why must cleaning liquids be kept away from children?
c: They can be harmful if swallowed or touched.
items.e: Look for warning symbols.

items.q: Priya looks at rain. Is this water solid or liquid?
c: It is a gas you can see.
items.e: Rain is liquid water.

items.q: Which state of matter can be squashed into a smaller space?
items.e: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow; gases spread out and can be squashed.

items.q: Which state of matter can be held in your hand without a container?
items.e: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow; gases spread out and can be squashed.

items.q: What happens when you stir sugar into warm water?
c: It dissolves and you cannot see it.
items.e: Sugar dissolves.

items.q: Does a solid change shape when you put it in a different box?
c: No. A solid keeps its shape.
items.e: Solids hold their shape.

items.q: Kai has a window. What is it made of?
items.e: A window is made of glass.

items.q: Which one is a solid?
items.e: Solids keep their shape.

items.q: Chloe has a plastic cup. What is it made of?
items.e: A plastic cup is made of plastic.

items.q: Kai has a crayon. What is it made of?
items.e: A crayon is made of wax.

items.q: Chloe sorts things. Which one can you see through?
items.e: The ice cube: see-through.

items.q: Mei sorts things. Which one is shiny?
items.e: The spoon: shiny.

items.q: Which state of matter forms a puddle when spilt?
items.e: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow; gases spread out and can be squashed.

items.q: Which state of matter keeps its own shape?
items.e: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow; gases spread out and can be squashed.

items.q: Which state of matter escapes from an open container?
items.e: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow; gases spread out and can be squashed.

items.q: Zoe sorts things. Which one bends easily?
items.e: The bouncy ball: bends.

items.q: Lucas sorts things. Which one sinks in water?
items.e: The rock: sinks.

items.q: Which state of matter flows and takes the shape of its container?
items.e: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow; gases spread out and can be squashed.

items.q: Which liquid flows fast?
items.e: Thin liquids flow fast.

items.q: Liam sorts things. Which one is soft?
items.e: The sock: soft.

items.q: What happens when you mix sand and water?
c: The sand sinks to the bottom.
items.e: Sand does not dissolve.

items.q: Hana sorts things. Which one feels rough?
items.e: The rock: rough.

items.q: Can a towel be twisted?
c: No, it is too hard or stiff.
items.e: Some materials can change shape easily; hard, stiff ones cannot.

items.q: Ethan tests a block made of wood. Which word fits it?
items.e: It is hard.

items.q: Which one sinks in water?
items.e: Heavy, small objects often sink.

items.q: Is turning a pipe cleaner round and round a pencil squashing, bending, twisting or stretching?
items.e: Squash: press. Bend: curve. Twist: turn. Stretch: pull longer.

items.q: Can a china plate be bent?
c: No, it is too hard or stiff.
items.e: Some materials can change shape easily; hard, stiff ones cannot.

items.q: Chloe tests an ice cube made of ice (frozen water). Which word fits it?

items.q: Is pulling an elastic band longer squashing, bending, twisting or stretching?

items.q: Which liquid flows slowly?
items.e: Thick liquids flow slowly.

items.q: Is curving a ruler made of thin plastic squashing, bending, twisting or stretching?
items.e: Squash: press. Bend: curve. Twist: turn. Stretch: pull longer.

items.q: Emma tests a sock made of cloth. Which word fits it?

items.q: Is pressing a sponge in your hand squashing, bending, twisting or stretching?
items.e: Squash: press. Bend: curve. Twist: turn. Stretch: pull longer.

items.q: Is curving a pipe cleaner into a U squashing, bending, twisting or stretching?
items.e: Squash: press. Bend: curve. Twist: turn. Stretch: pull longer.

items.q: Noah tests a rock. Which word fits it?
items.e: It sinks.

items.q: Can aluminum foil be twisted?
c: No, it is too hard or stiff.
items.e: Some materials can change shape easily; hard, stiff ones cannot.

items.q: Olivia tests a spoon made of metal. Which word fits it?
items.e: It sinks.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate chalk powder and water?
items.e: Use filtering because chalk is insoluble.

items.q: Which of these will NOT dissolve in water: bicarbonate of soda, cooking oil, salt or sugar?
items.e: Soluble materials dissolve; insoluble ones do not.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate tea leaves and tea?
items.e: Use filtering because the leaves do not dissolve.

items.q: Which solid can be poured?
items.e: Tiny solid pieces can be poured.

items.q: Which of these will NOT dissolve in water: bath salts, instant coffee granules, rice or salt?
items.e: Soluble materials dissolve; insoluble ones do not.

items.q: Bath salts: soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: Bath salts dissolves to make a solution.

items.q: Sawdust: soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: Sawdust does not dissolve, even when stirred.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate pebbles and soil?
items.e: Use sieving because pebbles are large.

items.q: Which of these will dissolve in water: bicarbonate of soda, chalk powder, cooking oil or flour?
items.e: Soluble materials dissolve; insoluble ones do not.

items.q: Marbles: soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: Marbles does not dissolve, even when stirred.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate steel pins and sawdust?

items.q: Bicarbonate of soda: soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: Bicarbonate of soda dissolves to make a solution.

items.q: Flour: soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: Flour does not dissolve, even when stirred.

items.q: Rice: soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: Rice does not dissolve, even when stirred.

items.q: Sugar: soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: Sugar dissolves to make a solution.

items.q: Pepper: soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: Pepper does not dissolve, even when stirred.

items.q: Which of these will NOT dissolve in water: gravel, jelly cubes (in hot water), powdered drink mix or salt?
items.e: Soluble materials dissolve; insoluble ones do not.

items.q: Which of these will dissolve in water: instant coffee granules, rice, sand or sawdust?
items.e: Soluble materials dissolve; insoluble ones do not.

items.q: Chalk powder: soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: Chalk powder does not dissolve, even when stirred.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate sand and water?
items.e: Use filtering because sand is insoluble and is caught by the filter paper.
